report_name: ConnectWise Cloud Backup Supply Chain Attack Hits M365 Tenants

attack_patterns.name: Additional Cloud Credentials
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor attempted to add new credentials to the ConnectWise Cloud Backup application's service principal within target tenants to establish persistence.

attack_patterns.name: Cloud Service Discovery
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor used the Microsoft Graph API to perform reconnaissance within compromised Microsoft 365 tenants to identify high-value targets and data.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor gained unauthorized access to customer data within Microsoft 365, including emails, OneDrive files, and SharePoint sites, by abusing the permissions of the compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup application.

attack_patterns.name: Password Spraying
attack_patterns.description: The same source IP address (144.172.64.128) used in the supply chain attack was also linked to password spraying campaigns against law firms on October 13 and 14, 2026.

attack_patterns.name: Supply Chain Compromise
attack_patterns.description: The attack was initiated by compromising a credential for a trusted third-party application, ConnectWise Cloud Backup, which was then used to access customer M365 environments.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor authenticated to the legitimate ConnectWise Cloud Backup OAuth application using a compromised credential to obtain access tokens for customer tenants.

tools.name: ConnectWise Cloud Backup
tools.description: A legitimate cloud backup application whose Microsoft 365 OAuth App credential was compromised and abused by threat actors to access customer tenants.

identities.name: ConnectWise
identities.description: Vendor of the compromised Cloud Backup application.

identities.name: Microsoft
identities.description: Vendor of the Microsoft 365 platform targeted in the attack.

identities.name: Huntress
identities.description: Security firm that reported on the impact of the supply chain attack.

identities.name: Microsoft 365 Tenants
identities.description: Customers of ConnectWise Cloud Backup whose Microsoft 365 environments were compromised. At least 173 tenants were impacted.

identities.name: Law Firms
identities.description: Victims of separate password spraying campaigns conducted from the same attacker IP address.

infrastructure.name: Attacker Source IP
infrastructure.description: The IP address from which all malicious activity, including the supply chain attack and separate password spraying campaigns, originated.

indicators.name: ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack Source IP

title: ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack Source IP
id: 2b1a9c8d-7e6f-4b5a-9d3c-1a2b3c4d5e6f
status: experimental
description: Detects network connections from the IP address associated with the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply chain attack.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/hackers-use-compromised-connectwise.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
  - attack.t1195
level: high
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationIp: '144.172.64.128'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects activity from the IP address 144.172.64.128, which was the source of the supply chain attack leveraging the ConnectWise Cloud Backup application.

indicators.name: Anomalous Sign-in to ConnectWise Cloud Backup App
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Sign-in to ConnectWise Cloud Backup App
id: 9e8d7c6b-5a4b-4c3d-2b1a-0f9e8d7c6b5a
status: experimental
description: Detects sign-ins to the ConnectWise Cloud Backup OAuth application (AppId 506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae) from the known malicious IP.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/hackers-use-compromised-connectwise.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
  - attack.t1078.004
  - attack.t1528
level: critical
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    AppId: '506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae'
    IpAddress: '144.172.64.128'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects suspicious sign-ins to the ConnectWise Cloud Backup OAuth application (AppId: 506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae), a key indicator of the supply chain attack.

indicators.name: Suspicious Credential Addition to Service Principal
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Credential Addition to Service Principal
id: 8d7c6b5a-4b3c-4d2b-1a0f-9e8d7c6b5a4b
status: experimental
description: Detects attempts to add new credentials to a service principal, a persistence technique observed in the ConnectWise supply chain attack.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/hackers-use-compromised-connectwise.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
  - attack.t1098.001
level: high
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: audit.azuread
detection:
  selection:
    Operation: 'Update ServicePrincipal'
    ModifiedProperties|contains:
      - 'KeyCredential'
      - 'PasswordCredential'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the addition of new credentials to a service principal, which was a persistence technique attempted by the actor in the ConnectWise supply chain attack.
